idiom_name: duck-typed visitor object plus a method-presence test in accept
implementation_notes: Neither the degenerate base nor declared interfaces are needed: a visitor is a plain object carrying only the methods for the elements it handles, and accept tests for the method - if (typeof visitor.visitCircle === 'function') visitor.visitCircle(this) - so the missing method is the failed cast of the classic form. What replaces the classic structure is this duck typing together with the prototype chain for the element hierarchy, and it makes partial visitation the natural shape of a visitor rather than a feature you build. Keep an explicit class hierarchy plus instanceof (or a documented visitor shape) when visitors are public API and you want the contract enforced and documented at the boundary.
pitfalls: A typo in the method name is indistinguishable from an unsupported element, so the presence test must be paired with a log or assertion; otherwise a visitor silently skips everything.
instanceof is per-realm: objects crossing an iframe, worker or vm boundary fail the check against this realm's constructors, which is why the method-presence test is the more portable dispatch test.
Nothing forces a new element to be handled: existing visitors keep loading and simply skip it, so without telemetry the regression is invisible until output goes missing.
